objectives: Write the formulae of compounds from the charges of ions.
Write and balance symbol equations including state symbols.
Write simple ionic equations for precipitation.
Check that atoms and charges balance.
reviewNotes: The list of ion charges is the standard school set; iron has two common ions (Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺).
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Common ions
blocks.md:
**1+**: H⁺, Na⁺, K⁺, Ag⁺, NH₄⁺. **2+**: Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu²⁺, Fe²⁺, Pb²⁺. **3+**: Al³⁺, Fe³⁺.
**1−**: Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, OH⁻, NO₃⁻. **2−**: O²⁻, S²⁻, SO₄²⁻, CO₃²⁻.

Compound formula: make the total positive charge equal the total negative charge (use brackets for groups): Al³⁺ + O²⁻ → **Al₂O₃**; Ca²⁺ + OH⁻ → **Ca(OH)₂**; NH₄⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → **(NH₄)₂SO₄**.

blocks.title: Balancing an equation
blocks.md:
1. Write the correct formulae (never change a formula to balance).
2. Count atoms of each element on both sides.
3. Put **coefficients** (numbers in front) to balance, one element at a time; leave hydrogen and oxygen until last.
4. Add **state symbols**: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) in water solution.

Example: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g).

blocks.title: Ionic equations
blocks.md: A precipitation reaction can be written showing only the ions that react. Silver nitrate + sodium chloride → silver chloride + sodium nitrate. Full: AgNO₃(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃(aq). Ionic: **Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → AgCl(s)**. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ are **spectator ions** (unchanged). Charges must balance as well as atoms.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.md:
- Subscripts (small numbers) belong to the formula; coefficients are the only thing you change.
- CO₂ ≠ CO₂² : never write charges on molecules.
- Always check both sides at the end by counting every element.

blocks.caption: Checking a balanced equation: iron and oxygen atoms are equal on both sides.
blocks.alt: The equation 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3 with atom counts for the left and right sides showing 4 iron and 6 oxygen on each side.

blocks.title: Example 1 — writing a formula
blocks.statement: Write the formula of (a) aluminium oxide and (b) calcium nitrate.
steps: (a) Al³⁺ and O²⁻: lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6: two Al³⁺ (6+) and three O²⁻ (6−) → Al₂O₃.
(b) Ca²⁺ and NO₃⁻: one Ca²⁺ needs two NO₃⁻ → Ca(NO₃)₂ (brackets round NO₃).

blocks.title: Example 2 — balancing
steps: Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe and 3 O. Make O even: 2Fe₂O₃ (4 Fe, 6 O) and 3O₂ (6 O).
Then 4 Fe on the left: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Check: Fe 4 = 4; O 6 = 6.
